exact_problem: Patients medically ready to leave stay in acute beds while health and care organisations coordinate onward care
key_evidence: ~324,000 bed days lost in Jan 2025; avg delay 6.1 days (REPORTED)
current_handling: Discharge hubs, transfer-of-care teams, trusted assessors
competitors: Care-coordination software, NHS digital discharge tools, consultancies
strongest_argument_against: Root cause is mostly social-care capacity (structural); public buyers with long cycles; tier-A wedge unclear

exact_problem: Theatre lists under-booked or finishing early, wasting scarce surgical capacity
key_evidence: 85% capped utilisation target; early finishes and under-booking main drivers (REPORTED)
competitors: Theatre scheduling software vendors, GIRFT (free), consultancies
strongest_argument_against: NHS-only buyer; national programme already targets it; no tier-A access

exact_problem: ~30% of HGV km run empty
current_handling: Backhaul boards, freight exchanges, fleet planners
competitors: Freight exchanges and load-matching platforms (not verified in this scan)
strongest_argument_against: Much empty running is structural (specialist vehicles, directional imbalance); crowded matching market

exact_problem: Generation/demand projects wait years for grid connection
key_evidence: >700 GW queue; >300 GW removed by reform (REPORTED)
strongest_argument_against: Reform restructuring the queue now; physical capacity is the bottleneck; tier C for operator

exact_problem: Applications to the Building Safety Regulator fail validation or stall for missing/poor design information, delaying high-rise projects
key_evidence: 44-56% failed validation (2025); delays of 12-18 months; ~1,500 decisions/yr now at 77-82% approval (REPORTED)
current_handling: Principal designers, fire engineers, specialist Gateway 2 consultancies
competitors: Gateway 2 consultancies; law firms; BSR guidance
strongest_argument_against: Regulator performance improving fast; low volume (~1,500/yr); life-safety domain requires specialists

exact_problem: Weak structured management practices associated with lower productivity
key_evidence: MES 2023 score 0.55; positive association after controls (REPORTED, ONS)
current_handling: Business-support programmes, consultants, Help to Grow
competitors: Consultancies, Help to Grow: Management, coaching
strongest_argument_against: Causal effect slow and hard to measure; low urgency; interventions are consulting

exact_problem: High turnover and unpaid travel time erode care capacity
competitors: Birdie, Access, CarePlanner and others (not verified)
strongest_argument_against: Buyers have thin margins set by council fees; safety-adjacent

exact_problem: Machines and lines deliver far below available capacity (availability, speed, quality losses)
key_evidence: Typical OEE ~60% vs 85% world class; Made Smarter reports 10-15% gains (REPORTED, programme/vendor)
current_handling: Lean consultants, MES/OEE tools, Made Smarter adoption support
competitors: OEE monitoring vendors, MES providers, Made Smarter
strongest_argument_against: Requires shop-floor access and sensor data (tier B); OEE norms are practitioner lore

exact_problem: Overproduction and forecast error create surplus and waste
strongest_argument_against: Much waste is process loss not forecasting; access needs plant data

exact_problem: Medication errors cause harm and cost
key_evidence: 237m errors/yr; £98m definitely avoidable ADE cost (REPORTED, academic)
strongest_argument_against: Safety-critical at proof stage

exact_problem: Service failures generate repeat contacts and lost staff time
competitors: Salesforce, Microsoft, Zendesk, Genesys, many AI-agent start-ups
strongest_argument_against: Hyper-contested by Big Tech and funded AI start-ups
status_v2: KILLED (K6: named incumbents; SME and enterprise segments both served)

exact_problem: ~20% of water put into supply leaks
strongest_argument_against: Monopoly buyers with regulated procurement; dense specialist incumbents

exact_problem: Councils pay high prices in a dysfunctional placement market
key_evidence: ~£5.7bn market; 22.6% profit for largest providers (REPORTED, CMA)
strongest_argument_against: Scarcity of placements is structural

exact_problem: Trusts pay different prices for identical products
current_handling: NHS Supply Chain, price benchmarking programmes
competitors: NHS Supply Chain, national price-transparency programmes
strongest_argument_against: National programmes own the data and mandate

exact_problem: Statutory assessments exceed the 20-week limit
strongest_argument_against: Driven by educational-psychologist shortage and demand (structural)

exact_problem: Waiting lists contain patients no longer needing care
key_evidence: £33 per validated removal; one trust removed 14,148 (REPORTED)
strongest_argument_against: Temporary incentive scheme; perverse-incentive risk

exact_problem: Working days lost to sickness
strongest_argument_against: Causal effect of interventions not attributable within any practical design

exact_problem: Spare-parts inventories hold obsolete and excess stock while critical parts stock out
strongest_argument_against: Vendor-only magnitude evidence

exact_problem: Mid-market firms hold the wrong inventory: excess slow stock alongside stock-outs, locking up cash and losing sales
key_evidence: UK NWC days up ~50% since 2015 (REPORTED, PwC, listed cos); OOS ~8% (academic)
competitors: Netstock, Slimstock, Inventory Planner, ERP planning modules (not individually verified)
strongest_argument_against: Crowded planning-software market; mid-market magnitude not evidenced independently

exact_problem: Retiring engineers take tacit maintenance knowledge with them
strongest_argument_against: Outcome not measurable as a standalone problem
status_v2: KILLED (K2; K9) - retained as a capability feature of maintenance arenas

exact_problem: Firms turn away work for lack of qualified staff
competitors: Dozens of AI accounting tools, offshore providers
strongest_argument_against: Vendor-sourced evidence; extremely crowded

exact_problem: Slow quotes lose orders in job-shop manufacturing
key_evidence: 67% of buyers expect a quote in 24h (REPORTED, vendor)
strongest_argument_against: Vendor-only; win-rate causation noisy

exact_problem: Out-of-stocks lose sales
strongest_argument_against: Enterprise buyers with strong incumbents

exact_problem: Businesses under-use flexibility markets
strongest_argument_against: Value per participant tiny

exact_problem: Record backlogs delay justice
strongest_argument_against: Judicial function; tier C
